subject: Closing the loop — Redwood + Acme (Discovery follow-ups)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>, Tom Brewer <tom.brewer@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood + Acme

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the next steps we agreed on: 

Summary (2–3 bullets):
- ACME uses generative summarization in product search; current latency and cost are high at scale.
- Primary constraints: P95 latency < 300ms for short queries, data residency in us-west, and SOC2 compliance review.
- Current RFP timeline: decision window lining up with Q1 budget planning (target Jan).

Agreed next steps:
1) I’ll send a lightweight pricing preview and a short architecture note on Dedicated vs Hosted sizing (attached).
2) Marcus will follow up with a throughput/latency runbook sample and recommend a pilot config.
3) You’ll confirm the list of technical stakeholders (SDK + infra) and provide a target date for a pilot start.

Open questions:
- Any compliance docs we should share ahead of SOC2 checklist? (we can share redacted audit artifacts).
- Expected concurrent request volume for search (ballpark).

Attachment: redwood-pricing-preview.pdf (pdf)

If this looks right I’ll circle back next week to lock dates for a pilot kickoff.

Best,
Marissa

No rush — just checking on prioritization so we can plan capacity on our end.

Hi Alice —

Looping in Lauren (our AE lead) so she’s aware of timing. We’re trying to finalize Q1 pilot slots — if ACME is still planning to move forward, can you confirm whether you want us to hold a slot in mid-Jan? If the project’s lower priority, totally understand — please let us know so we don’t block capacity.

If easier, a one-line reply with your current prioritization is perfect.

Thanks again,

Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Closing the loop — Redwood + Acme (should I close the file?)

Hi Alice —

Hope you’re well. I haven’t heard back on the pilot timing or a prioritization note, so I wanted to close the loop. Should I close the file on our end for now? We’re happy to re-open and schedule a pilot when the timing is right — no hard feelings.

Quick options: reply with one of the below replies and I’ll act accordingly:
- “Hold” — please hold a Q1 mid-Jan slot and we’ll coordinate stakeholders
- “Later” — not a priority, please close the file and feel free to re-open when ready
- “Proceed” — we’re greenlit and want a kick-off in Jan (I’ll send a calendar invite)

If I don’t hear back by end of next week I’ll mark this as inactive and free up capacity.

Thanks for the time — and if there’s anything small we can do to help move this forward (sample pilot SOW, compliance artifacts, or a short demo), say the word.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Closing the loop — Redwood + Acme (should I close the file?)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for checking in and for the helpful follow-ups. We liked Redwood a lot in the discovery, but we’ve deprioritized the project for Q1 given other roadmap commitments. Please close the file for now; I’ll reach back out when we’re ready to re-engage (likely mid-2027).

Appreciate the materials and the time — feel free to leave the pricing preview on file.

Best,
Alice
Senior Product Manager
Acme Enterprises
